request.notes: The EXACT agent lookup behind the operator-identity guard (REQUIREMENTS §5C.5). Takes `id` and nothing else (additionalProperties: false — see _tools_snapshot.json). Chosen over lithos_agent_list because the list filters archived registrations by default while this lookup answers for them: an archived agent's id must not read as unregistered, or the registration that follows would silently re-type that agent as a human.

observed_divergences: The ABSENT answer is a bare JSON `null`, not an error envelope: the tool is documented "Agent info dict or None if not found" (live tools/list description, vendored in _tools_snapshot.json), unlike lithos_agent_archive, which answers an `agent_not_found` envelope. That is why `variants.absent` is `null` — the one non-object response any vendored contract carries, and the only variant the well-formedness guard exempts — and why `mcp_transport.decode_tool_result` gives it its own code (NULL_RESULT_CODE) for `LithosClient.agent_info` to map to None. A fake answering whatever the client expected would have hidden it (PRD clarification 2, Dave 2026-10-03). SCOPE NOTE, not a divergence: the payload carries `first_seen_at`, `archived_at` and `metadata` as well as the three fields Lens reads; `normalize_agent`/`AgentRecord` model `id`, `name`, `type` and `last_seen_at` only, which is the documented round-trip scope boundary in README.md — the guard's whole question is the TYPE, and the archive state it does not model is precisely what this tool (unlike the list) still answers for. `make contracts-verify` against a live Lithos remains the step that checks the request shape on the wire; it has not been run from the build environment that added this contract, which could reach no Lithos.
